questions.stem: Why is aqueous electrolysis more complex than molten electrolysis?

options.text: Because the water evaporates too quickly
Because water provides additional H⁺ and OH⁻ ions, giving a choice of which ion is discharged at each electrode
Because the electrodes dissolve in water
Because aqueous solutions cannot conduct electricity

questions.explanation: In aqueous electrolysis, water partially dissociates into H⁺ and OH⁻ ions. This means there are four types of ions present (two from the compound, two from water), and at each electrode there is a choice of which ion is discharged. Rules based on reactivity and concentration determine which ion is preferentially discharged.
